Scope placement changes observable answers even among candidates with the same question hash. For a known distributor and a known unoffered component, node.142f34016b300f5c110eb249 and node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b can return FALSE, while node.2a6321b4ce90763bf0be564e returns OUT_OF_SCOPE. Node.97af37a2579f59b0ee43211f also places the offered-and-linked condition in scope. These are not runtime-equivalent alternatives; the intended distinction between not caught and out of scope needs resolution.

Scope differences also affect incomplete evidence. Under the declared runtime semantics, an unknown scope returns UNKNOWN even where a known non-gift or qualifying discount would make a corresponding unscoped prohibition conjunction FALSE. This is an executable distinction, not evidence that the circular imposes an additional legal restriction.

The offer-level candidates node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 and node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 combine offer-level promotional linkage with existence of a non-discount gift component. The source says, "If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product". Unless the fact contract establishes that the identified gift participates in the linked promotion, the formula can combine a product-linked component with a different, unlinked gift and overstate the restriction. Whether an offer-wide link suffices remains unresolved.

The offer-level existential facts require complete enough component evidence to support FALSE. Node.968dbccb08282a4e8a580ae5 expressly states, "False requires sufficient evidence that no offered component meets both conditions; unresolved classification remains unknown." Node.bca408c75cbf8467afafada6 does not expressly state this completeness condition. Its generic UNKNOWN semantics do not themselves implement component enumeration or prevent an incorrectly supplied FALSE.

A fee or charge discount is an exception to the selected gift restriction, not a general permission under the circular. Likewise, node.6d6e7adc6faa9d94b74c08e5's TRUE_IS_COMPLIANT result is confined to the selected gift control. Reading either as overall legality would omit the independently supported advertising and section 103 duties.

The source states that guaranteed returns or other incentives "may be considered a gift" in db43e253bea18.u12.2646. Their classification must remain individual and unresolved where evidence is insufficient. The representations generally preserve this qualification; no automatic gift classification or blanket permission for guaranteed returns follows from these checks.

Node.bc55be7e973a689d07f9e64b distinguishes the offeror from whoever funds or fulfils a benefit. The source's wording "distributors should not offer any gifts" supports focusing on offering rather than receipt. However, it does not independently resolve disputed attribution, agency or third-party arrangements. Those remain classification questions, not implemented conclusions.

The circular defines distributors by reference to intermediaries distributing SFC-authorised funds in db43e253bea18.u0.2, while its quotation of paragraph 3.11 uses the broader words "a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product". Fund-specific candidate definitions can fit this circular's selected scope, but their equivalence to the full Code provision outside that scope is not established.

The supplied units do not establish an effective interval for the candidates' stated temporal basis. The explicit date 30 September 2010 identifies the FAQ cited in footnote 3; it is not an effective date for every rule or dependency. Applicable versions and competing temporal interpretations remain unresolved.

The declared global CONFLICT blocking and UNKNOWN propagation are supplied runtime conventions, not requirements derived from the circular. They preserve uncertainty but should not be described as legal prohibitions or permissions.
